title: Ambiguous JSON detector and rewrite fallback for customer tool invocations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several customers (AcmePayments, HelixHealth, and a smaller enterprise partner on Dedicated) reported mis-parsed function/tool call outputs in production. Symptoms include truncated JSON objects, JSON objects merged across adjacent responses, and occasional parser errors that cause the customer request to fall back to text output. Incidents occurred across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and correlate with: 1) streaming + retry via the private proxy, 2) KV-cache hits that produce zero-length early flushes, and 3) proxy-side reassembly during high concurrency.
steps_to_reproduce: Enable streaming tool/function calling on a multi-turn chat route (use sample function that returns JSON).
Configure proxy to simulate a retry during partial body transmission (network delay + retry).
Send burst of requests with mix of cache-hit and cold-start to reproduce interleaving behavior.
Observe parser errors or merged JSON objects in the assembled stream when using current streaming framing implementation.
root_cause: Race condition in the streaming reassembly layer + ambiguous framing when early / zero-length chunks are emitted by the KV cache optimization. The reassembly code reuses a per-worker sequence counter that, under proxy retry and connection reuse, can collide across requests and cause adjacent chunks to be stitched together without a proper boundary marker. Parser then receives concatenated JSON fragments with no clear separator leading to invalid JSON or merged objects.
proposed_fix: Introduce request-scoped UUID framing token for every streaming frame so boundaries are unambiguous even with retries/connection reuse.

Add a tolerant rewrite fallback in the parser: when a top-level JSON parse fails, attempt a single-pass heuristic split on framing tokens and balanced-brace recovery to extract best-effort objects and surface structured errors to the customer rather than raw text.
Ensure KV-cache fast-path cannot emit zero-length flush frames; if a zero-length is needed, emit an explicit empty-frame token instead of relying on implicit boundaries.
Add unit and integration tests that simulate proxy retries, connection reuse, and mixed cache-hit/cold-start traffic.
work_done: Initial reproducer built in local dev cluster (Diego) using a proxy emulator that can inject partial-body retries.
Kernel-level change scoped to streaming reassembly to add per-request UUID token (PR opened).
Parser fallback heuristic prototype implemented and run against customer traces to validate extractions.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout to hosted us-west-2 (5% traffic) with extended structured-output monitoring for 24h.
If canary is healthy, expand to all hosted regions and then schedule Dedicated ring upgrade during next maintenance window.
For Private deployments, provide patch and checklist for operators (notes in docs).
qa_plan: Add synthetic tests that feed known-challenging customer traces through both old and new framing + parser.
Fuzz input generator for streaming frames to exercise boundary cases and retries.
Coordinate with solutions engineering to run patch on a non-production Dedicated cluster for customer repro validation.

notes: Trade-offs: adding framing tokens slightly increases bytes on wire but removes ambiguity and reduces customer-request SLO misses. Parser fallback increases CPU cost on error paths; we gate it behind a rollout flag for the initial deployment.
Follow-ups: audit other streaming code paths for implicit boundary assumptions (embeddings, reranking).
Customer communications: Drafted postmortem and mitigation steps for HelixHealth and AcmePayments; coordinating with customer success for replay and verification.
